jp: 大事[だいじ]な約束[やくそく]を忘[わす]れ{てしまいました|pt-teshimau}。
en: I forgot an important appointment (and I regret it).
why: てしまう expresses regret or an unintended outcome: something happened that the speaker did not want.

jp: 財布[さいふ]を電車[でんしゃ]に忘[わす]れ{ちゃった|pt-teshimau}。
en: Oops, I left my wallet on the train.
why: ちゃう is the casual contraction of てしまう and marks an unwanted slip.

jp: ケーキを一人[ひとり]で全部[ぜんぶ]食[た]べ{てしまいました|pt-teshimau}。
en: I ate the whole cake by myself (and feel bad about it).
why: てしまう marks an action that ended up fully done or went too far, often with a feeling of regret.

jp: 携帯電話[けいたいでんわ]を落[お]として、壊[こわ]し{てしまいました|pt-teshimau}。
en: I dropped my phone and broke it.
why: てしまう expresses regret or an unintended outcome: something happened that the speaker did not want.

jp: 寝坊[ねぼう]して、授業[じゅぎょう]に遅[おく]れ{てしまった|pt-teshimau}。
en: I overslept and ended up late for class.
why: てしまう expresses regret or an unintended outcome: something happened that the speaker did not want.

jp: 母[はは]の大切[たいせつ]なお皿[さら]を割[わ]っ{てしまいました|pt-teshimau}。
en: I broke my mother's precious plate.
why: てしまう expresses regret or an unintended outcome: something happened that the speaker did not want.

jp: 傘[かさ]を持[も]たずに出[で]かけたら、雨[あめ]に降[ふ]られ{てしまった|pt-teshimau}。
en: I went out without an umbrella and ended up getting rained on.
why: てしまう expresses regret or an unintended outcome: something happened that the speaker did not want.

jp: この漫画[まんが]は面白[おもしろ]くて、一晩[ひとばん]で読[よ]ん{でしまいました|pt-teshimau}。
en: This comic was so interesting that I ended up reading it in one night.
why: てしまう marks an action that ended up fully done or went too far, often with a feeling of regret.

jp: 言[い]ってはいけないことを言[い]っ{てしまいました|pt-teshimau}。
en: I said something I should not have said.
why: てしまう expresses regret or an unintended outcome: something happened that the speaker did not want.

jp: 電車[でんしゃ]で寝[ね]{てしまって|pt-teshimau}、降[お]りる駅[えき]を通[とお]り過[す]ぎました。
en: I fell asleep on the train and (unintentionally) passed my station.
why: てしまう expresses regret or an unintended outcome: something happened that the speaker did not want.

jp: 風邪[かぜ]をひい{てしまいました|pt-teshimau}ので、今日[きょう]は休[やす]みます。
en: I have caught a cold, so I will take the day off.
why: てしまう marks an unwelcome event that has happened (catching a cold).

jp: 昨日[きのう]は疲[つか]れて、シャワーも浴[あ]びずに寝[ね]{ちゃった|pt-teshimau}。
en: I was tired yesterday and went to bed without even showering.
why: ちゃう is the casual form of てしまう and marks an outcome the speaker did not intend.

jp: 辞書[じしょ]をなくし{てしまいました|pt-teshimau}。
en: I have lost my dictionary.
why: てしまう expresses regret or an unintended outcome: something happened that the speaker did not want.

jp: 友達[ともだち]の秘密[ひみつ]を、つい人[ひと]に話[はな]し{ちゃった|pt-teshimau}。
en: I accidentally told someone my friend's secret.
why: つい ('without meaning to') goes naturally with てしまう, here in its casual form ちゃう.

jp: 大切[たいせつ]にしていたコップを落[お]とし{てしまった|pt-teshimau}。
en: I dropped the glass that I had treasured.
why: てしまう expresses regret or an unintended outcome: something happened that the speaker did not want.

jp: 先月[せんげつ]もらった給料[きゅうりょう]を、もう全部[ぜんぶ]使[つか]っ{てしまった|pt-teshimau}。
en: I have already spent all of last month's pay.
why: てしまう marks an action that ended up fully done or went too far, often with a feeling of regret.

jp: 明日[あした]の会議[かいぎ]の資料[しりょう]を、間違[まちが]えて消[け]し{てしまいました|pt-teshimau}。
en: I deleted tomorrow's meeting materials by mistake.
why: てしまう expresses regret or an unintended outcome: something happened that the speaker did not want.

jp: 子[こ]どもは疲[つか]れて、ソファで寝[ね]{てしまいました|pt-teshimau}。
en: The child got tired and fell asleep on the sofa.
why: てしまう can mark something that happens against one's control, like falling asleep.

jp: 彼[かれ]の話[はなし]を聞[き]いて、思[おも]わず泣[な]い{てしまいました|pt-teshimau}。

why: 思わず ('involuntarily') calls for てしまう.

jp: 間違[まちが]えて、知[し]らない人[ひと]にメールを送[おく]っ{てしまいました|pt-teshimau}。
en: I sent an email to a stranger by mistake.
why: てしまう expresses regret or an unintended outcome: something happened that the speaker did not want.

jp: 試験[しけん]の日[ひ]を間違[まちが]え{てしまいました|pt-teshimau}。
en: I got the date of the exam wrong.
why: てしまう expresses regret or an unintended outcome: something happened that the speaker did not want.

jp: 熱[あつ]いお茶[ちゃ]を飲[の]んで、舌[した]をやけどし{ちゃった|pt-teshimau}。
en: I drank hot tea and burned my tongue.
why: ちゃう, the casual form of てしまう, marks an accident the speaker did not want.

jp: 電池[でんち]が切[き]れ{てしまいました|pt-teshimau}。
en: The battery has run out.
why: An event that just happened and is inconvenient takes てしまう; 切れる is intransitive.

jp: 急[いそ]いでいたので、鍵[かぎ]をかけずに家[いえ]を出[で]{てしまいました|pt-teshimau}。

why: てしまう expresses regret or an unintended outcome: something happened that the speaker did not want.

jp: あっ、ガムを踏[ふ]ん{じゃった|pt-teshimau}。

why: じゃう (after ん) is the casual form of でしまう and marks an unwanted accident.

jp: まだ見[み]ていない映画[えいが]の結末[けつまつ]を、聞[き]い{ちゃった|pt-teshimau}。
en: I heard the ending of a movie I haven't seen yet, unfortunately.
why: ちゃう, the casual form of てしまう, marks something unwelcome that happened against the speaker's wish.

jp: ティッシュをポケットに入[い]れたまま、洗濯機[せんたくき]で洗[あら]っ{てしまいました|pt-teshimau}。
en: I left a tissue in my pocket and ended up washing it in the machine.

jp: 楽[たの]しい時間[じかん]は、あっという間[ま]に過[す]ぎ{てしまいます|pt-teshimau}。
en: Happy times are over before you know it.

jp: 寒[さむ]いと、つい布団[ふとん]から出[で]られなくなっ{てしまいます|pt-teshimau}。
en: When it is cold, I inevitably can't get out of my futon.
why: つい plus an unintended result takes てしまう.

jp: ごめん、借[か]りた本[ほん]を汚[よご]し{ちゃった|pt-teshimau}。
en: Sorry, I got the book I borrowed dirty.
why: ちゃう is the casual form of てしまう and expresses regret, here in an apology.

jp: 子[こ]どもの頃[ころ]に住[す]んでいた家[いえ]は、もう壊[こわ]され{てしまった|pt-teshimau}。
en: The house I lived in as a child has already been torn down.
why: てしまう can express a regretful, irreversible change.

jp: 大事[だいじ]な書類[しょるい]を、うっかり捨[す]て{てしまいました|pt-teshimau}。
en: I threw out an important document by mistake.
why: てしまう expresses regret or an unintended outcome: something happened that the speaker did not want.

jp: 彼[かれ]は私[わたし]に何[なに]も言[い]わずに、行[い]っ{てしまった|pt-teshimau}。
en: He left without telling me anything.
why: てしまう can mark a departure that cannot be undone and that the speaker regrets.

jp: 道[みち]に迷[まよ]っ{てしまって|pt-teshimau}、約束[やくそく]の時間[じかん]に遅[おく]れました。
en: I got lost and was late for the appointment.
why: てしまう expresses regret or an unintended outcome: something happened that the speaker did not want.

jp: 犬[いぬ]が庭[にわ]から逃[に]げ{てしまいました|pt-teshimau}。
en: The dog ran away from the garden.
why: てしまう expresses regret or an unintended outcome: something happened that the speaker did not want.
